name: Actionability Guidance (Diet, Supplements, Labs)
purpose: Pack-authored lifestyle and follow-up guidance keyed by gene. Applied only when matching markers appear in the curated pack report with the listed severity/interpretation filters.
implementation_note: This file is the source of truth for dashboard Diet / Supplements / Labs. Do not hardcode parallel rules in the UI. Every item is conditional guidance, never a diagnosis, prescription, permanent elimination diet, or medication instruction. Soft genetic context must yield to allergies, medical diets, pregnancy/lactation context, medications, labs, and clinician orders (see meal_planning_rules.json).
disclaimer: Educational suggestions only. Not medical advice. Confirm symptoms, labs, medications, and clinical context before changing diet or supplements.

safety_notes: More markers increase coverage, not certainty or personal disease probability.
Do not start, stop, or change a medication from raw DNA alone; use a current CPIC/FDA/label-supported PGx result with a clinician or pharmacist.
Do not start high-dose supplements or impose long-term food exclusions from a common SNP alone.
A safety concern can be more important than a wellness suggestion: review allergies, pregnancy/lactation, kidney/liver disease, eating-disorder risk, and medication interactions first.

Total Iron Binding Capacity (TIBC)

favor: Iron-containing foods that fit the person's diet while the reason for an abnormal iron result is clarified
avoid: Treating an iron-status marker as proof of iron deficiency, iron overload, or anemia
Starting or avoiding iron supplements from fatigue or a single SNP without iron studies and clinical context
supplements: Iron supplementation only after reviewing ferritin, transferrin saturation, CBC, bleeding or dietary history, and clinician or pharmacist guidance

lab_tests.name: Complete blood count (CBC)
Ferritin and transferrin saturation
Serum iron, TIBC, or transferrin when clinically indicated

rules.notes: TMPRSS6 and TF markers can modestly shift population iron or hemoglobin traits, but they do not distinguish deficiency, blood loss, inflammation, kidney disease, diet, or iron overload in an individual. Menstrual or other bleeding, gastrointestinal history, pregnancy, medications, and measured iron studies are more informative than a common SNP.

favor: Lactose-free alternatives
Fermented dairy (kefir, organic Greek yogurt)
avoid: Cow milk
Ice cream
Soft unaged cheeses

avoid: Alcohol
Acetaldehyde exposure

lab_tests.name: Liver Enzyme Panel (ALT/AST)

rules.notes: Some ALDH2-associated patterns are linked to slower acetaldehyde clearance after alcohol exposure. Use personal symptoms, exposure history, and clinician guidance; this is not a cancer diagnosis or a fixed personal threshold.

favor: Alcohol-free options when alcohol causes flushing, tachycardia, nausea, headache, sleep disruption, or other adverse effects
avoid: Alcohol when it causes flushing, tachycardia, nausea, headache, sleep disruption, or other adverse effects
Using a possibly protective ADH1B association to justify heavier drinking or dismiss alcohol-related risk
rules.notes: ADH1B rs1229984 can alter ethanol-to-acetaldehyde conversion and may be associated with drinking-pattern phenotypes, but the result is not an alcohol-use-disorder prediction or a safe-drinking threshold. Interpret with ALDH2, actual exposure, symptoms, medications, liver status, body size, and personal or cultural context.

Montmorency tart cherry juice
Low-fat organic dairy
avoid: High-purine foods (organ meats, shellfish)
Beer
High-fructose corn syrup

favor: Wild fish
Egg yolks
UV-irradiated mushrooms

Using a vitamin-D pathway genotype to choose a dose or claim vitamin D deficiency

Ionized Calcium & PTH

Allium vegetables (garlic, onions)

favor: Magnesium-rich foods (pumpkin seeds, dark chocolate)
Cruciferous vegetables
avoid: Excessive caffeine
Chronic sleep deprivation

lab_tests.name: Salivary Cortisol Rhythm (4-point)

avoid: Caffeine after 12:00 PM
High-dose caffeine stimulants
rules.notes: Caffeine response varies. Use sleep, anxiety, blood-pressure, pregnancy, medication, and personal-response context; this marker does not establish a fixed personal limit.

favor: Use caffeine timing, dose, sleep, anxiety, heart-rate, and blood-pressure response logs to personalize caffeine choices
avoid: High-dose or late-day caffeine when sleep, anxiety, palpitations, or blood-pressure symptoms worsen
Treating an ADORA2A marker as proof of an anxiety disorder or a universal caffeine limit
rules.notes: ADORA2A rs5751876 may modify caffeine-related arousal, anxiety, or sleep response, especially under caffeine exposure. Combine it with CYP1A2, timing, dose, smoking, medications, pregnancy status when relevant, and observed response; no genotype establishes a universal cutoff.

Arugula & leafy spinach
Pomegranates

Seafood
Sunflower seeds

lab_tests.name: Selenium level (blood)

favor: B12-containing foods or fortified foods that fit the person's diet and goals
Use measured B12 status, symptoms, dietary pattern, and medication context before deciding whether supplementation is worth discussing
avoid: Treating a FUT2, TCN2, or CUBN marker as proof of vitamin B12 deficiency
Using folate or an energy formula to cover unresolved B12-related symptoms without checking the underlying cause
supplements: A B12 supplement only after reviewing diet, measured status, medications, total intake, and clinician or pharmacist guidance
medication_context: Metformin and acid-suppressing medicines can be part of a B12 review; do not stop or change them from raw DNA.

lab_tests.name: Complete blood count (CBC) with MCV
Serum or plasma vitamin B12
Methylmalonic acid (MMA) when B12 status is borderline or clinically uncertain
Homocysteine with folate and kidney context when clinically indicated

rules.notes: FUT2, TCN2, and CUBN markers can point to a B12-status or absorption question, but effects are modest and overlapping causes are common. Serum B12, CBC, symptoms, diet, medication exposure, kidney function, and—when appropriate—MMA or homocysteine are more informative than a common SNP.

lab_tests.name: Clinical BRCA1/2 NGS Confirmation Panel
Breast MRI / Mammography Referral

rules.notes: Requires professional genetic counseling support.

lab_tests.name: Clinical Lynch Syndrome NGS Confirmation Panel
Colonoscopy Screening Referral

rules.notes: Requires professional genetic counseling support.

medication_context: If this raw-array finding is confirmed, review the exact contraceptive or hormone product (including whether it contains estrogen) and personal/family VTE history with a clinician; do not change medication from this report.

lab_tests.name: Clinical Factor V Leiden / prothrombin mutation confirmation

rules.notes: This is a confirmation and medication-context prompt, not a recommendation to screen everyone or a diagnosis of current thrombosis.

favor: A balanced eating pattern built around fiber-rich foods, adequate protein, and minimally processed carbohydrate sources
Regular physical activity progressed gradually to fit current ability, symptoms, and recovery
avoid: Treating a common metabolic SNP as a diabetes diagnosis or as a reason to start medication
Using a highly restrictive diet to chase a genotype without symptom, lab, medication, or clinician context

lab_tests.name: HbA1c
Fasting plasma glucose

rules.notes: Common metabolic markers shift average risk by small or context-dependent amounts. Use symptoms, family history, body-composition context, medications, and laboratory testing rather than a SNP to assess glucose status.

favor: A balanced, fiber-forward eating pattern and regular movement
If triglycerides or liver tests are elevated, discuss reducing sugar-sweetened beverages and frequent alcohol exposure
avoid: Assuming normal blood lipids rule out fatty-liver susceptibility
Using detox products or high-dose supplements as liver treatment

lab_tests.name: Fasting lipid panel including triglycerides
HbA1c
ALT/AST/GGT liver panel
Liver ultrasound or FibroScan when clinically indicated

rules.notes: GCKR, APOA5, PNPLA3, and TM6SF2 findings can point to different lipid, glucose, and liver phenotypes. They do not diagnose fatty liver, steatohepatitis, pancreatitis, or diabetes; measured labs and clinical evaluation lead.

favor: Use hunger, fullness, meal timing, sleep, and activity observations to personalize meal structure
Build meals around satisfying protein- and fiber-containing foods that fit the person's goals and dietary requirements
avoid: Treating an MC4R association as an obesity diagnosis, a willpower judgment, or a fixed calorie target
Using a satiety marker to justify extreme restriction or unmonitored weight-loss medication use
rules.notes: MC4R rs17782313 is associated with modest appetite/adiposity differences in some studies. Personal hunger, sleep, medications, environment, body-composition trajectory, and many other genes are more informative; the marker does not diagnose obesity or select a diet or medication.

favor: Use a heart-healthy eating pattern and regular activity as general cardiovascular foundations
Review measured Lp(a), ApoB, LDL-C, triglycerides, blood pressure, and family history together rather than reading one SNP in isolation
avoid: Assuming a protective-leaning LDL-pathway marker removes the need for lipid monitoring
Using a genotype as a substitute for measured lipids and global cardiovascular-risk assessment
medication_context: Do not start, stop, or change a statin, PCSK9 medicine, aspirin, or other cardiovascular therapy from raw DNA; review measured Lp(a), ApoB, LDL-C, medical history, and clinician guidance.

lab_tests.name: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] blood test (at least once if not previously measured)
ApoB (Apolipoprotein B)
Standard lipid panel (LDL-C, HDL-C, triglycerides)
Blood pressure measurement

rules.notes: LPA and LDL-pathway markers can suggest a reason to check the phenotype, but they do not quantify risk or determine treatment. Lp(a), ApoB, LDL-C, triglycerides, blood pressure, family history, and clinical risk assessment remain decisive.

avoid: High-dose iodine or selenium supplements without clinical guidance

lab_tests.name: TSH
Free T4
Thyroid antibodies when autoimmune thyroid disease is clinically suspected

medication_context: Do not start, stop, or change levothyroxine or another thyroid medicine from a common SNP; review symptoms, exact medication, TSH, free T4, and clinician assessment together.
rules.notes: Common thyroid-pathway markers are hypothesis prompts only. Thyroid function, autoimmunity, pregnancy/postpartum context, iodine and selenium exposure, and medication response require phenotype and clinical testing.

favor: A consistent sleep opportunity and wake-time routine that fits the person's work, caregiving, and health needs
A brief sleep and daytime-alertness diary when sleep timing or quality is a concern

lab_tests.name: Sleep study when snoring, witnessed apneas, gasping, or daytime sleepiness warrant evaluation

medication_context: Do not use a chronotype or sleep-duration SNP to justify sedatives, stimulants, or a medication change; review sleep symptoms, substances, medicines, and clinician assessment.
rules.notes: Common sleep markers may provide small chronotype or sleep-duration context. They do not diagnose insomnia, sleep apnea, natural short sleep, or a treatment response.

favor: An exposure and symptom log that records the food or environment, timing, objective symptoms, and co-factors
avoid: Permanent food elimination or unsupervised food challenge based only on a genetic marker

lab_tests.name: Allergist-directed skin or specific-IgE testing when the exposure history fits

medication_context: Do not use an AOC1, HNMT, or immune SNP to label a food allergy or to change antihistamine, asthma, or emergency medicines; use an allergist-directed plan when indicated.
rules.notes: Food allergy, intolerance, histamine symptoms, eczema, and asthma are different clinical questions. DNA can provide limited pathway context but cannot identify a safe food, diagnose allergy, or rule out anaphylaxis.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical CYP2C19 phenotype review when clopidogrel is being considered

medication_context: If clopidogrel is being considered or already used, show this report to the prescriber or pharmacist; a validated clinical CYP2C19 phenotype may inform antiplatelet selection, but a consumer-array call cannot select, stop, or switch therapy.
rules.notes: Clopidogrel decisions require a complete clinical CYP2C19 interpretation plus the cardiovascular indication, other medicines, and clinician judgment.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical CYP2C9/VKORC1/CYP4F2 review with INR monitoring when warfarin is being considered

medication_context: If warfarin is being considered or already used, review a validated clinical result with the prescriber; INR, indication, interacting medicines, diet, and ongoing monitoring remain essential, and raw DNA cannot determine a dose or justify a medication change.
rules.notes: CPIC warfarin guidance uses a complete clinical genotype-to-phenotype interpretation together with non-genetic dosing and monitoring factors.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical statin-PGx review when statin-associated muscle symptoms or a statin decision is active

medication_context: If a statin is being considered or already used, especially simvastatin, discuss a validated clinical result with the prescriber and report muscle pain, weakness, or dark urine; do not stop, select, or change a statin from raw DNA.
rules.notes: Statin-associated musculoskeletal symptoms depend on the complete clinical result, statin, dose, interactions, medical history, and symptoms.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical CYP2D6 phenotype review when codeine or tramadol is being considered

medication_context: If codeine or tramadol is being considered or already used, a complete clinical CYP2D6 phenotype may identify situations where an alternative is preferred; do not select, avoid, or change an opioid from raw SNP data.
rules.notes: Opioid recommendations are drug-specific and phenotype-specific; pain indication, age, other medicines, and safer non-opioid options also matter.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical CYP2D6 and medication-interaction review when tamoxifen is being considered

medication_context: If tamoxifen is being considered or already used, bring this report and the complete medication list to the oncology team; do not alter endocrine therapy or stop another medicine because of raw DNA.
rules.notes: Tamoxifen decisions require oncology context, complete CYP2D6 interpretation, and review of CYP2D6-inhibiting medicines; a consumer-array result is not sufficient.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical antidepressant-PGx review when an SSRI or related antidepressant question is active

medication_context: If an SSRI, SNRI, or related antidepressant is being considered or already used, a validated clinical phenotype may inform a prescribing discussion; do not start, stop, or change psychiatric medication from raw SNP data.
rules.notes: CPIC distinguishes gene-drug guidance with clinical evidence from genes or outcomes that do not support routine prescribing use; medication response also depends on diagnosis, symptoms, interactions, and patient preference.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical PGx diplotype/phenotype review for the specific gene and medication

medication_context: If a medication question is active, record the exact drug, indication, dose, timing, benefit, side effects, and other medicines; a single consumer SNP is not a complete PGx diplotype, phenotype, or dose recommendation.
rules.notes: Use current CPIC, FDA labeling, or an equivalent clinical laboratory report for gene-drug interpretation. A clinical PGx result can inform prescribing, but raw consumer-array data cannot independently clear, select, or dose a medication.

lab_tests.name: Clinical DPYD genotype/phenotype confirmation before fluoropyrimidine therapy

medication_context: If fluorouracil (5-FU) or capecitabine is being considered, show this finding to the oncology team before treatment; do not use a raw-array call to choose a dose or to change therapy.
rules.notes: DPYD findings can be clinically important for fluoropyrimidine toxicity, but high-stakes decisions require a validated clinical result and oncology interpretation.

lab_tests.name: Clinical TPMT/NUDT15 genotype or enzyme-activity review before thiopurine therapy

medication_context: If azathioprine, mercaptopurine, or thioguanine is being considered, the prescriber should review a validated TPMT/NUDT15 result and monitoring plan; do not select or change a thiopurine dose from raw DNA.
rules.notes: TPMT and NUDT15 status can inform thiopurine starting-dose decisions in clinical care, while other disease, monitoring, and treatment factors remain important.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical HLA typing for the specific drug-risk allele

medication_context: Before abacavir, carbamazepine/oxcarbazepine, or allopurinol is prescribed, use the appropriate clinical HLA result and prescriber guidance; a consumer SNP proxy cannot clear or contraindicate the drug by itself.
rules.notes: HLA-B*57:01, HLA-B*15:02, HLA-A*31:01, and HLA-B*58:01 have drug-specific clinical relevance. The medication decision is drug- and allele-specific and requires validated HLA typing.

lab_tests.name: Quantitative G6PD enzyme activity and/or validated clinical G6PD genotype review

medication_context: If rasburicase, dapsone, primaquine, methylene blue, or another oxidative-stress medication is being considered, the prescriber needs validated G6PD status; do not self-stop or self-start a medicine from a raw SNP.
rules.notes: G6PD medication risk depends on the clinical phenotype, variant, drug, dose, illness, and other oxidative stressors. A limited SNP set cannot rule out deficiency.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical HLA-B*57:01 typing before abacavir is considered

medication_context: If a validated clinical HLA-B*57:01 result is positive and abacavir is being considered, the prescribing team should follow current HIV/CPIC guidance and select an appropriate alternative; do not start, stop, or switch abacavir from this report.
rules.notes: HLA-B*57:01 is a drug-specific abacavir hypersensitivity marker. A consumer-array label or inferred HLA result is not equivalent to validated clinical HLA typing.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical HLA-B*15:02 and HLA-A*31:01 review before carbamazepine or oxcarbazepine is considered

medication_context: If carbamazepine or oxcarbazepine is being considered, the prescriber should review validated HLA-B*15:02 and HLA-A*31:01 status and current CPIC guidance, especially before first exposure; do not start, stop, or switch an aromatic anticonvulsant from this report.
rules.notes: HLA-B*15:02 and HLA-A*31:01 have drug- and allele-specific cutaneous hypersensitivity relevance. A negative consumer-array proxy does not clear risk, and a positive label requires validated HLA interpretation.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical HLA-B*58:01 typing before allopurinol is considered

medication_context: If allopurinol is being considered, the prescriber should review validated HLA-B*58:01 status before initiation; a positive result requires alternative-therapy review under current CPIC guidance. Do not start, stop, or switch allopurinol from this report.
rules.notes: HLA-B*58:01 is drug-specific context for allopurinol severe cutaneous adverse reactions. A consumer-array proxy cannot clear or establish this risk without validated clinical HLA testing.

lab_tests.name: Clinical RYR1/CACNA1S malignant-hyperthermia susceptibility evaluation when indicated

medication_context: Before surgery, tell the anesthesia team about a confirmed or suspected malignant-hyperthermia finding or relevant family history; a consumer-array result cannot clear susceptibility or choose an anesthetic plan.
rules.notes: Only validated pathogenic-variant or contracture-test context supports malignant-hyperthermia susceptibility management. Composite gene labels are matched by their individual gene symbols.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical CYP2C9 diplotype/phenotype review when an NSAID such as ibuprofen, celecoxib, meloxicam, naproxen, or diclofenac is being considered
Kidney function/eGFR and blood-pressure review when regular or repeated NSAID use is being considered

medication_context: If an NSAID is being considered for menstrual or other pain, a complete clinical CYP2C9 phenotype may inform a drug-specific discussion; kidney, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, bleeding-risk, pregnancy, and interacting-medication context still matter. Do not start, stop, select, or dose an NSAID from raw-array data.
rules.notes: CPIC reports moderate-to-high evidence linking CYP2C9 genotype with exposure to several NSAIDs, but evidence for many direct treatment-response or adverse-event outcomes is weaker. This does not diagnose NSAID intolerance or make an NSAID unsafe for everyone.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical CYP3A5 diplotype/phenotype review when tacrolimus is being considered in transplant care
Tacrolimus whole-blood trough / therapeutic-drug monitoring when tacrolimus is prescribed

medication_context: If tacrolimus is being considered or already used in transplant care, bring the complete clinical CYP3A5 result, transplant details, interacting medicines, organ function, and trough-monitoring plan to the transplant team. A consumer-array call cannot determine a tacrolimus dose or justify a medication change.
rules.notes: CPIC links CYP3A5 genotype to tacrolimus exposure and target-trough achievement, while noting that genotype-guided dosing has not established improved long-term clinical outcomes. This pathway is not a general kidney-health or wellness finding and is relevant only to active clinical tacrolimus care.

lab_tests.name: Plasma pseudocholinesterase activity and dibucaine number or validated BCHE clinical testing when an anesthesia history or BCHE finding warrants review

medication_context: If there is a personal or family history of prolonged paralysis or apnea after succinylcholine or mivacurium, or a confirmed BCHE finding, tell the anesthesia team before surgery. BCHE risk can be inherited or acquired, and a consumer-array call cannot clear risk or choose an anesthetic plan.
rules.notes: BCHE deficiency is often silent until exposure to susceptible neuromuscular blockers. Clinical enzyme activity, dibucaine testing, history, and validated genetic testing are more informative than a limited consumer SNP set.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical UGT1A1 repeat/diplotype review before irinotecan therapy
CBC with neutrophil monitoring and liver-function review as directed by the oncology team when irinotecan is used

medication_context: If irinotecan is being considered or used, the oncology team should review the complete clinical UGT1A1 result, including promoter-repeat testing when relevant, the regimen, liver function, blood counts, and monitoring plan. A raw-array proxy cannot select or change an irinotecan dose.
rules.notes: UGT1A1*28 and *6 context can contribute to irinotecan toxicity risk, but clinical significance depends on complete variant/haplotype testing, regimen, dose, ancestry, and patient factors. These markers do not diagnose Gilbert syndrome or predict toxicity from a proxy alone.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical NAT2 diplotype/acetylator-phenotype review when hydralazine is being considered or used
Blood-pressure, symptom, and clinician-directed monitoring review during hydralazine care

medication_context: If hydralazine is being considered or already used for resistant hypertension, heart failure, or another clinical indication, a complete NAT2 phenotype may inform the prescriber’s review of exposure, response, adverse effects, and follow-up. Do not start, stop, or change hydralazine from raw-array data.
rules.notes: The 2025 CPIC guideline links NAT2 phenotype with hydralazine exposure and response, while emphasizing complete diplotype interpretation and clinical monitoring. Consumer SNPs cannot assign rapid, intermediate, poor, or indeterminate NAT2 phenotype by themselves.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical CYP2C19 diplotype/phenotype review when omeprazole, lansoprazole, pantoprazole, or dexlansoprazole is being considered

medication_context: If a first-generation proton-pump inhibitor or dexlansoprazole is being considered or used, a complete clinical CYP2C19 phenotype may inform the prescriber’s discussion of exposure and treatment response; indication, duration, interactions, and measured symptoms still matter. Do not start, stop, select, or dose a PPI from raw-array data.
rules.notes: CPIC reports stronger CYP2C19 evidence for omeprazole, lansoprazole, pantoprazole, and dexlansoprazole than for esomeprazole or rabeprazole, for which the guideline makes no recommendation. A single SNP cannot establish a CYP2C19 phenotype or a treatment decision.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical CYP2B6 diplotype/phenotype review when efavirenz is being considered or used in HIV care

medication_context: If efavirenz is being considered or used, the HIV prescriber should review a complete clinical CYP2B6 phenotype, current HIV guidance, treatment history, and adverse effects; do not start, stop, or change an efavirenz regimen or dose from raw-array data.
rules.notes: CPIC links CYP2B6 phenotype with efavirenz exposure and CNS-adverse-effect context, but the CYP2B6*6 component alone cannot assign a complete phenotype or prescribe a dose. This pathway is limited to clinical efavirenz care.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical CYP2C9 diplotype/phenotype review before phenytoin is considered

medication_context: If phenytoin is being considered or used, the prescriber should review a validated CYP2C9 phenotype, relevant HLA-B*15:02 status, serum-level monitoring, interactions, and clinical response because phenytoin has a narrow therapeutic index. Do not start, stop, or dose phenytoin from raw-array data.
rules.notes: CPIC links CYP2C9 genotype with phenytoin exposure and includes HLA-B*15:02 severe cutaneous adverse-reaction context. A limited consumer-array result cannot establish the complete phenotype, clear HLA risk, or determine a phenytoin dose.

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical HLA-B*15:02 typing before phenytoin is considered

medication_context: If phenytoin is being considered and a validated clinical HLA-B*15:02 result is positive, the prescriber should follow current CPIC guidance before initiation; a consumer-array label cannot clear severe cutaneous-reaction risk or choose an alternative anticonvulsant.
rules.notes: HLA-B*15:02 is drug-specific severe cutaneous adverse-reaction context for phenytoin. This exact allele requires validated HLA testing and must not be inferred from a broad HLA gene match or a missing consumer-array call.

favor: Adequate protein and calcium-rich or fortified foods that fit the person's diet, plus weight-bearing or resistance activity when safe
Track low-trauma fractures, height loss, bone pain, steroid exposure, relevant menstrual or menopause or hormone-therapy context, and family history before interpreting a bone marker
avoid: Using a bone SNP to diagnose osteoporosis, predict a fracture, or prescribe calcium, vitamin D, or hormone therapy
High-dose calcium or vitamin D, unmonitored bone-building products, or abrupt changes to activity or medication without measured and clinical context
supplements: Review calcium, vitamin D, magnesium, vitamin K, and any bone-health product against diet, kidney or stone history, medications, and measured status with a clinician or pharmacist; a genotype does not establish need or dose

lab_tests.name: DXA/BMD assessment when indicated by age, fracture history, risk factors, or clinician assessment
25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], calcium, phosphate, PTH, and alkaline phosphatase when bone or mineral symptoms or risk factors warrant
Kidney function and medication review when calcium, vitamin D, or bone therapy is being considered

medication_context: Review glucocorticoids, thyroid replacement, anticonvulsants, aromatase inhibitors, androgen or estrogen therapy, and osteoporosis medicines with a clinician; do not start, stop, or change them from raw DNA.
rules.notes: Bone density and fracture decisions differ by age, sex, menopause or hormone status, body context, medications, prior fracture, and clinical risk. Common variants are modest context only; DXA and clinical evaluation lead when indicated. This route supports different bodies without inferring anatomy or current hormone levels.

favor: Use a symptom, stool, food, and medication log that records bleeding, pain, fever, weight change, nocturnal symptoms, and exposure timing
Maintain adequate hydration and nourishment using tolerated foods, and ask a gastroenterology clinician or dietitian before restrictive elimination plans
avoid: Using an IBD-associated SNP to diagnose Crohn disease or ulcerative colitis, decide that symptoms are IBS, or start steroids, biologics, or immune-suppressing treatment
Long-term restrictive diets, probiotics, digestive enzymes, or detox products as treatment based only on DNA
supplements: Do not use an IBD marker to choose iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium, or another supplement; review measured deficiencies, possible malabsorption, kidney or liver status, and medicines with a clinician or pharmacist

lab_tests.name: Complete blood count (CBC) and iron studies when anemia, bleeding, or malabsorption is a concern
C-reactive protein (CRP) and fecal calprotectin when inflammatory bowel disease is clinically suspected
Stool infection evaluation, GI consultation, endoscopy, or imaging when symptoms and clinician assessment warrant

medication_context: Review frequent NSAID use and every current medicine with a clinician if GI symptoms or bleeding occur; a genotype does not establish NSAID safety.

Do not self-treat, stop, or change prescribed digestive or immune medicines from raw DNA; persistent diarrhea, blood, weight loss, fever, nocturnal symptoms, anemia, or significant pain warrants clinical evaluation.
rules.notes: IBD susceptibility is polygenic and interacts with immune, microbiome, environmental, and clinical factors. The NOD2, ATG16L1, IL23R, FCGR2A, and IL10 markers are hypothesis prompts only; blood, stool, endoscopy or imaging, and a clinician's differential diagnosis lead.

avoid: Beginning lifelong gluten avoidance solely because HLA-DQ2 or HLA-DQ8 is permissive, especially before discussing diagnostic testing if celiac disease is suspected
Using a consumer SNP tag as a substitute for clinical HLA typing, celiac serology, or biopsy

lab_tests.name: tTG-IgA and total IgA while celiac disease is being evaluated
EMA-IgA or appropriate IgG-based testing when clinically indicated, followed by duodenal biopsy when warranted
Clinical HLA-DQ2/DQ8 typing when a clinician uses genetic testing to clarify celiac disease likelihood

medication_context: If celiac disease is suspected, discuss testing before removing gluten because a gluten-free diet can affect test interpretation; do not diagnose or change medicines from an HLA context marker.
rules.notes: HLA-DQ2/DQ8 permissiveness is common and is not a celiac diagnosis. This panel is a prompt to verify what the consumer array can and cannot resolve, then use symptoms, serology, gluten exposure, and clinician-directed testing.

favor: Bring the panel label, fracture history, dental or hearing findings, height or skeletal history, and family history to a bone specialist or clinical geneticist when the clinical picture fits
avoid: Using a consumer-array panel flag to diagnose or exclude osteogenesis imperfecta, clear high-impact activity, or start, stop, or select bone medication
supplements: Review calcium, vitamin D, and other bone products against measured status, kidney or stone history, current medicines, and the clinical evaluation; the panel does not establish a supplement need or dose

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical bone-fragility gene-panel or sequencing review when phenotype and family history warrant
DXA/BMD and mineral-lab assessment when indicated by fracture history, symptoms, age, or clinician assessment

medication_context: If a rare bone-fragility disorder is suspected, review glucocorticoid exposure, osteoporosis medicines, planned procedures, and activity restrictions with the treating team; do not change treatment from a consumer-array panel result.
rules.notes: The panel target represents a route to validated clinical testing, not a positive result in the consumer file. Osteogenesis imperfecta and related bone-fragility disorders require phenotype, imaging, family history, and clinically interpreted sequencing; common SNPs cannot rule them in or out.

favor: If persistently low alkaline phosphatase, recurrent stress or atypical fractures, chronic bone pain, early tooth loss, or nephrocalcinosis is present, bring the history and panel label to an endocrinology, metabolic-bone, dental, or genetics clinician
avoid: Treating low alkaline phosphatase as hypophosphatasia, taking extra vitamin B6 as a diagnostic test, or starting enzyme, bone, calcium, or vitamin-D treatment from a consumer-array panel flag
supplements: Tell the clinician about pyridoxine or vitamin B6, calcium, vitamin D, and other supplements before confirmatory testing; do not stop a prescribed product or change a dose without clinical advice

lab_tests.name: Repeat serum alkaline phosphatase interpreted with age, sex, liver, pregnancy, fracture, and medication context when hypophosphatasia is suspected
Specialist-directed serum PLP (vitamin B6), mineral, and urine phosphoethanolamine evaluation when indicated
Validated clinical ALPL sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis when phenotype and laboratory findings warrant

medication_context: If hypophosphatasia is suspected, disclose vitamin B6 products and all bone medicines to the clinician because they can affect interpretation or management; do not self-start, stop, or change treatment from raw DNA.
rules.notes: Hypophosphatasia is evaluated using compatible clinical features, persistently low alkaline phosphatase interpreted for age and context, relevant substrate testing, and clinically interpreted ALPL testing. A consumer panel label is not a diagnosis and a single low enzyme result has multiple possible explanations.

favor: If severe, reproducible symptoms follow fructose, sucrose, sorbitol, or sucralose exposure, record the exposure, timing, symptoms, hydration, and medical history and discuss the panel label with a metabolic clinician or dietitian
avoid: Performing a fructose challenge, using a common FODMAP result as a hereditary-fructose-intolerance diagnosis, or adopting a highly restrictive diet solely from a consumer-array panel flag

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical ALDOB sequencing with deletion/duplication analysis when the exposure-linked phenotype warrants
Clinician-directed glucose, liver-function, and metabolic evaluation after severe exposure-linked symptoms

medication_context: If hereditary fructose intolerance is suspected, tell the treating team before medicines, oral products, or nutrition plans are changed because ingredient and exposure review is clinical; do not use raw DNA to self-diagnose or manage an acute reaction.
rules.notes: Hereditary fructose intolerance is rare and requires an exposure-linked clinical picture plus biallelic clinically interpreted ALDOB pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, or specialist-directed biochemical confirmation. Fructose challenge testing can be dangerous and must not be suggested by this tool.

favor: If unexplained thickened heart muscle, heart-failure symptoms, rhythm or conduction problems, progressive neuropathy, autonomic symptoms, bilateral carpal-tunnel history, or a relevant family history is present, bring this marker label to a cardiology or amyloidosis specialist
avoid: Using a consumer-array signal to diagnose amyloidosis, assume ancestry or age-based certainty, or start, stop, or select cardiac or amyloidosis treatment

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical TTR genotyping and variant-classification review
ECG, echocardiogram, cardiac biomarkers, cardiac MRI, or nuclear cardiac imaging only when cardiology indicates

medication_context: If the variant is clinically confirmed, cardiology should interpret it with symptoms, imaging, family history, age, and other causes of amyloidosis; do not self-start, stop, or change a heart or amyloidosis medicine from raw DNA.
rules.notes: TTR p.Val142Ile is associated with late-onset hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with age-dependent and incomplete penetrance. A consumer-array observation requires validated clinical testing and phenotype; a positive result is not proof of current disease, and a negative result does not exclude other TTR or non-TTR disease.

favor: If exertional fainting, palpitations, known cardiomyopathy, unexplained ventricular rhythm problems, or sudden cardiac death in the family is present, bring the panel label and history to an inherited-cardiomyopathy team
avoid: Using a consumer-array panel flag to clear endurance or high-intensity exercise, decide on an ICD, or start, stop, or select a cardiac medicine

lab_tests.name: Clinical cardiomyopathy gene-panel or sequencing review with expert variant classification
ECG, ambulatory rhythm monitoring, echocardiogram, or cardiac MRI when cardiology indicates

medication_context: If an inherited cardiomyopathy is suspected, let the cardiology team determine activity, medication, and family-evaluation plans from phenotype, imaging, rhythm data, and clinically interpreted variants; raw DNA cannot provide exercise or treatment clearance.
rules.notes: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy is a clinical and imaging diagnosis in which variant classification, family history, rhythm findings, ventricular function, and exercise exposure may matter. This exact panel target is a route to clinical evaluation, not a positive consumer-array result.

favor: Bring the exact variant label, personal and family cancer history, and prior screening history to a genetic counselor or clinician when a CHEK2 finding is being considered
avoid: Treating a raw CHEK2 signal as a cancer diagnosis, assuming BRCA-level risk, or changing screening, surgery, or cancer treatment without clinical confirmation and variant-specific counseling

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical CHEK2 sequencing with deletion/duplication and variant-classification review
Genetic counseling and family-history-based screening plan after clinical confirmation

medication_context: If a CHEK2 pathogenic variant is clinically confirmed, the care team should interpret screening and any cancer-treatment questions using the exact variant, family history, tumor context, and current guidelines; do not change medication from raw DNA.
rules.notes: CHEK2 risk is moderate and variant-specific. Truncating, missense, and uncertain variants must not be collapsed into one risk estimate; a consumer indel or SNP call is not a clinical classification and a negative result does not erase hereditary-cancer risk from other genes or family history.

favor: Bring the exact MUTYH label, colorectal-polyp or cancer history, family history, and any prior colonoscopy information to a genetic counselor or gastroenterology clinician
avoid: Calling one raw MUTYH allele a diagnosis of MUTYH-associated polyposis, assuming biallelic status without phase testing, or changing colonoscopy or cancer care from consumer DNA alone

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical full-gene MUTYH sequencing with deletion/duplication, zygosity, and phase review
Genetic counseling and clinician-directed colorectal screening plan after confirmation

medication_context: If MUTYH-associated polyposis is clinically confirmed, screening and treatment decisions belong with genetics and gastroenterology teams; raw DNA cannot select a medicine or replace endoscopic and family-history context.
rules.notes: MUTYH-associated polyposis is primarily a biallelic/compound-heterozygous question. A single consumer call may represent carrier status, a false positive, or an incomplete view of the gene; clinical sequencing and phase/zygosity interpretation are required.

favor: Bring this ancestry-sensitive APC label, family history, and colonoscopy history to a genetic counselor or clinician if colorectal screening questions apply
avoid: Treating APC I1307K as classic familial adenomatous polyposis, a cancer diagnosis, or an automatic colonoscopy or treatment instruction without clinical confirmation and ancestry-aware counseling

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical APC testing and ancestry-aware variant interpretation
Clinician-directed colorectal screening review using family history and current guidelines

rules.notes: APC I1307K is distinct from the high-penetrance APC variants that cause classic familial adenomatous polyposis. Associations vary by ancestry and clinical context; a consumer result is not a diagnosis or a stand-alone screening schedule.

favor: If prostate screening is relevant to your anatomy or care goals, bring this ancestry-sensitive HOXB13 label, family history, and prior PSA history to a clinician or genetic counselor
avoid: Using a raw HOXB13 result to diagnose prostate cancer, assume risk is the same across ancestries, or begin, stop, or change screening or treatment without clinical confirmation and shared decision-making

lab_tests.name: Validated clinical HOXB13 testing and variant interpretation when clinically indicated
Clinician-directed PSA and prostate-risk discussion when relevant to the person's anatomy, age, and family history

medication_context: If a clinically confirmed HOXB13 finding changes a prostate-risk discussion, the clinician should integrate age, family history, ancestry, PSA history, and shared goals; do not change hormone or cancer treatment from raw DNA.
rules.notes: HOXB13 G84E is a prostate-cancer susceptibility association with ancestry-dependent frequency and risk. It is not diagnostic, does not infer anatomy or identity, and does not replace individualized PSA or clinical risk discussion.

favor: If mood, behavior, pain, or need-for-space symptoms appear cycle-linked, record daily symptoms, bleeding, sleep, stress, medication timing, and symptom-free days across at least two cycles
avoid: Calling a late-luteal or menstrual symptom pattern an estrogen spike, diagnosing PMDD from a panel, or selecting an SSRI, hormone, supplement, or contraceptive change from raw DNA
medication_context: If symptoms cause meaningful impairment, discuss the prospective diary and exact medication or contraceptive label with a clinician; evidence-based options depend on the symptom pattern, goals, interactions, contraindications, and product, not on this research panel.
rules.notes: This panel is research context for possible sensitivity to normal ovarian-steroid change, not a measurement of estrogen, progesterone, allopregnanolone, or a PMDD diagnosis. Cyclic irritability, avoidance, anger, anxiety, depression, or pain should be evaluated as a recurring phenotype with safety review and appropriate clinical care.

favor: If ovarian, cycle, androgen, fertility, or metabolic questions apply, record cycle regularity, symptoms, relevant medications, sleep, activity, nutrition, and the person's goals without assuming anatomy or fertility plans
avoid: Using a research panel to diagnose PCOS, infer ovulation or fertility, prescribe a calorie target, or start, stop, or select metformin, contraceptive, antiandrogen, or hormone treatment

lab_tests.name: Clinician-directed cycle/ovulation and androgen evaluation when the person's symptoms and goals warrant
HbA1c, fasting glucose, lipid panel, or other metabolic testing when clinically indicated

medication_context: Discuss the exact hormone or metabolic product label and treatment goal with the prescriber or pharmacist; PCOS care is individualized and cannot be chosen from a consumer-array panel.
rules.notes: PCOS is a clinical and laboratory diagnosis with overlapping phenotypes and different care goals. This panel is a reproductive-metabolic research context prompt and cannot establish PCOS, current hormone levels, ovulation, fertility, or medication response.

favor: If pelvic pain, painful periods, pain with sex, bowel or bladder pain, or fertility questions apply, record timing, severity, bleeding, functional impact, and medication use for a gynecology or primary-care discussion
avoid: Using an endometriosis research panel to diagnose or exclude endometriosis, infer fertility, or start, stop, or choose hormonal, pain, or surgical treatment
medication_context: Bring the symptom diary and exact product labels to the clinician; pain and hormonal treatment require review of pregnancy possibility, contraindications, kidney/liver status, bleeding risk, interactions, and personal goals rather than DNA alone.
rules.notes: Endometriosis susceptibility associations are not diagnostic and do not explain the cause or severity of one person's pain. Clinical history, examination, imaging when indicated, and specialist assessment lead; consumer DNA cannot substitute for that workup.

favor: If heavy or prolonged bleeding, worsening period pain, pelvic pressure, or pain with sex is present, bring a dated symptom and bleeding record to a gynecology clinician
avoid: Treating an adenomyosis research-gap record as a diagnosis, assuming a hormone cause from DNA, or changing contraception, hormone therapy, pain treatment, or supplements from this signal

lab_tests.name: CBC and ferritin when bleeding is heavy or prolonged or anemia symptoms are present
Pelvic examination and transvaginal ultrasound or MRI when clinically indicated

medication_context: Use the exact contraceptive or hormone label and discuss benefits, bleeding effects, alternatives, and contraindications with the prescriber; raw DNA cannot identify adenomyosis or select a treatment.
rules.notes: Adenomyosis remains an evidence gap for consumer SNP interpretation. Research loci and hormonally responsive tissue biology do not diagnose or exclude the structural uterine condition; symptoms, examination, imaging, and gynecology review are required.
